quarterly_data.signal: H1 FY2026 (January-June 2026) results: net sales JPY 2,274.5 billion (up 3.5%), a record for the period, led by mirrorless and network cameras; gross profit JPY 1,122.9 billion (up 8.4%) and gross margin 49.4% (up 2.3 points) despite cost increases from surging memory prices, helped by refunds of US additional tariffs and the weaker yen; operating profit JPY 230.6 billion (up 7.6%); net income attributable to Canon shareholders JPY 171.2 billion (up 9.8%). Segments: Printing sales JPY 1,239.9 billion (up 1.5%); Medical JPY 277.4 billion (down 0.7%), as defects in a production-system switchover and a supplier hit by a disaster delayed parts procurement; Imaging JPY 552.7 billion (up 16.9%). H1 R&D expenses JPY 177.2 billion; no material change to the planned capex.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 2,274.5 billion (+3.5%); operating profit JPY 230.6 billion (+7.6%); gross margin 49.4%

quarterly_data.signal: Industrial Business Unit H1 FY2026: sales JPY 145.2 billion (down 9.1%; optical equipment JPY 107.5 billion, down 3.8%; industrial equipment JPY 36.1 billion, down 21.9%), pre-tax profit JPY 18.8 billion (down 31.5%). Management states semiconductor lithography demand is on a rising trend for memory and generative AI, but sales fell because they are concentrated in the second half; FPD lithography sales fell because panel makers delayed investment decisions last year to assess the US additional tariffs. Management describes the semiconductor equipment market as led by generative-AI demand as AI-related investment expands.
